ai.body: AI polishing is optional and off by default. Configure your own AI service on its dedicated settings page. If a polishing request exceeds five seconds, Talkless quietly keeps the recognized text.

dictionary.title: Names worth getting right.
dictionary.body: Add your names, projects, and everyday vocabulary. Tell Talkless how a word is often misheard, and that spelling is fixed every time—even without AI polish. Confirmed spellings stand out in the live transcript.

privacy.local.title: Local speech stays local.
privacy.local.body: With local Qwen and Enhanced recognition off, audio is processed on your Mac, not uploaded. Download the speech model separately, then dictate offline.
privacy.cloud.title: Cloud is a choice, not a catch.
privacy.cloud.body: Online recognition uses Volcengine’s Doubao Speech ASR API, an external service relative to Talkless, not the Doubao chat app. Audio goes directly to Volcengine. Optional AI polishing, editing and translation use your separately configured AI provider.
privacy.history.title: Your history lives with you.
privacy.history.body: Dictation history and diagnostic logs stay on your Mac. Logs are bounded to 15 MB and exclude audio, transcripts, API keys, and prompts. Nothing is automatically uploaded.
privacy.open.title: An app you can look inside.
privacy.open.body: Talkless is source available and distributed directly on GitHub. The app does not collect telemetry. This website has no analytics or tracking scripts; its host may keep standard request logs.
faq.title: A few good questions.
faq.mac.q: Will it work on my Mac?
faq.mac.a: Talkless requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later. Intel Macs and older macOS versions aren't supported. The current release is a beta, so expect a few rough edges.
faq.setup.q: What does getting started look like?
faq.setup.a: Install Talkless in Applications. In the setup guide, confirm your microphone first, then choose your dictation key and hold or tap mode. Configure Offline or Doubao in Settings → Voice input. AI polishing is optional and has its own settings page.
faq.offline.q: Do I need an account or a subscription?
faq.offline.a: No Talkless account is required. Local recognition runs on your Mac after the model download, with no hosted Talkless service. If you choose cloud speech or AI features, bring your own provider credentials and check that provider's pricing and privacy policy.
faq.apps.q: Does it replace my keyboard or input method?
faq.apps.a: Neither. Talkless lives in the menu bar and inserts text into the field you're using. Keep that field focused until the result arrives. Some apps restrict text insertion or access to selected text; the user guide explains the controls and limitations.
faq.language.q: Can I use it in English and Chinese?
faq.language.a: The app interface supports English and Simplified Chinese. Recognition language support depends on your selected speech engine and model. Optional AI translation and output language settings are separate from the interface language.
faq.help.q: Where do I find help or report a bug?
faq.help.a: Start with the user guide for setup and shortcuts. Our support page covers common problems and what to include when reporting a bug.

guide.meta.title: User guide — Talkless
guide.meta.description: Install Talkless, set up local speech recognition, and learn the dictation, polishing and translation controls.
guide.eyebrow: A SMALL GUIDE TO GETTING STARTED
guide.title:
From a thought
to a text field.
guide.intro: Start with local dictation. Add cloud speech or AI only if you want them. No Talkless account is needed.
guide.install.title: Install and prepare
guide.install.first: Use an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later. Download the beta, open the DMG, and drag Talkless into Applications. Open that copy of the app.
guide.install.permissions: The setup guide starts by confirming your microphone and its permission, then lets you customize the dictation key and hold or tap mode. Accessibility enables global shortcuts and text insertion; skipping setup does not grant permissions.
guide.install.model: In Settings → Voice input, choose Offline and download the local Qwen3 ASR · 0.6B model (about 713 MB). Wait for verification and preparation to finish. Model weights are separate from the app and are not hosted by Talkless. App updates do not require downloading the model again.
guide.shortcuts.title: Speak and finish
guide.shortcuts.body: Click a text field, hold your dictation key, speak, and release. In tap mode, press once to start and again to finish. Configure both in Settings → Voice input or Setup Guide. A speaking pause does not stop recording; Escape cancels.
guide.shortcuts.focus: Keep the intended text field focused until the result arrives. Talkless uses a queued clipboard paste, not an input method. It keeps the text available for a short compatibility interval before restoring your previous clipboard, unless you copied something else. Posting paste keys does not prove the destination accepted the text. Finished results remain in History.
guide.shortcuts.keys: Fn is the default, not a requirement. Change the key in Voice input settings. If Fn opens the emoji panel, set the Globe-key action to Do Nothing in macOS Keyboard settings, or choose another key. Settings opens from the menu bar, without a Command-comma shortcut.
guide.speech.title: Choose your speech engine
guide.speech.body: In Settings → Voice input, choose Offline or Doubao online. Offline uses the local model; previews periodically reprocess accumulated audio and the final pass covers the complete recording, with safe internal windows for long audio. Doubao uses your Speech API key and ASR 2.0 resource. Auto keeps live recognition; a specific input language uses the supported streaming-input endpoint and may return text later. Spoken cleanup is a separate Doubao option, not AI polishing. The menu bar offers engine and online-language switches. Optional offline fallback requires a downloaded model.
guide.speech.mic: The microphone is first in Voice input settings. System default shows the actual device; it means the default audio input, not direct capture of your Mac's playback. A specific missing device is not silently replaced. Capture failures or a three-second gap in audio callbacks cancel quietly; ordinary silent buffers do not. Start a new dictation after checking the device.
guide.ai.title: Use AI only when you want it
guide.ai.body: Settings → AI polishing contains its switch, provider, credentials, model and writing preferences. It is off by default and separate from recognition. Polishing requests have a five-second deadline; timeout quietly uses the recognized text. Settings → Text formatting controls local punctuation and spacing without an AI service.
guide.ai.more: Voice editing is enabled on the AI polishing page: select text, hold the dictation key with Control (Option if your key is Right Control), and speak an edit. The dictation key alone types. Translation defaults to Control-Option-T and has its own language settings. Review output before relying on it.
guide.dictionary.title: Keep useful words and results
guide.dictionary.body: Settings → Dictionary shows each entry as heard → written. Talkless learns on its own: when AI polish keeps making the same spelling fix, that fix takes effect automatically, and it retires after 30 days without use, for example once recognition gets the word right. Learned words also become recognition hints, so mistakes get rarer over time. Add your own entries too; they never retire. Everything stays on your Mac. Blue dictionary marks mean the spelling appears in the text, not that a correction is guaranteed. Your own entries can be imported and exported as plain text.
guide.dictionary.history: History keeps up to 500 recent results on your Mac. Search, copy or delete entries there, or use Copy Last Result in the menu bar menu. Clearing history and clearing daily activity are separate actions. Interface language, recognition language and AI output language are separate settings too.
privacy.meta.title: Privacy — Talkless
privacy.meta.description: What stays on your Mac, what optional providers receive, and how Talkless stores credentials, history and diagnostics.
privacy.page.title:
Local by default.
Specific about the rest.
privacy.page.intro: Local-first is a starting point, not a blanket promise that every feature is offline. Here is how the app and this website handle data.
privacy.audio.title: Speech and model downloads
privacy.audio.body: Local Qwen processes audio on your Mac. Model downloads contact your chosen source; Talkless does not host weights. Online recognition uses the Doubao Speech ASR API offered through Volcengine, not the Doubao chat app or Volcano Ark chat-model API. Audio is sent directly to that service, including when Labs Enhanced recognition is enabled. Talkless does not relay or save recordings.
privacy.requests.title: Optional AI requests
privacy.requests.body: AI polishing sends transcript text, dictionary hints and writing instructions to your configured provider. Enhanced recognition can send both local and online transcripts for comparison; sentence alternatives uses the same service. App-aware tone can include the foreground app and its writing context. Output-language and additional instructions apply when configured. Voice editing sends selected text and the spoken instruction; translation sends selected text and language instructions.
privacy.requests.choice: Opening AI settings does not send your text. Fetch Models and Test Connection are explicit network actions; a connection test uses a fixed sample, not your dictation. Provider pricing, processing and retention policies apply. Talkless cannot guarantee a provider’s privacy practices.
privacy.storage.title: History and credentials
privacy.storage.body: Preferences and dictionary entries use macOS UserDefaults. AI service keys and the dedicated Doubao Speech key use macOS Keychain. Retired cloud-provider keys are never reused for Doubao; older plaintext credentials may remain from previous versions.
privacy.storage.history: Models, text history, text-free daily totals and diagnostics live in your Mac’s Library/Application Support/Talkless folder. History contains text, not audio, and holds up to 500 results. Delete saved text in History; clear daily activity separately. Daily totals are retained for 400 calendar days.
privacy.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics you choose to share
privacy.diagnostics.body: Event logs are bounded to 15 MB and exclude audio, transcripts, API keys and prompts. Export diagnostics creates a local ZIP; it does not upload it. Optional macOS crash reports can contain personal information and file paths. Inspect an export before sharing it.
privacy.website.title: This website and distribution
privacy.website.body: The app does not collect telemetry. This website has no analytics, tracking scripts, remote fonts or microphone access. Its host may keep standard request logs. The demo uses sample text in your browser. The language preference is stored locally when available.
privacy.website.download: Download buttons use this site’s /download address, then redirect to the published GitHub release asset. GitHub handles that download under its own policies. Talkless is source available: you can inspect the repository from the single GitHub link in the header. This wording does not grant a software license.

support.meta.description: Troubleshoot permissions, speech models, text insertion and AI connections, and prepare a useful Talkless bug report.
support.eyebrow: WHEN SOMETHING GETS IN THE WAY
support.title:
Let’s get your
words moving again.
support.intro: Try the checks below first. They cover the most common reasons a dictation does not start or reach your text field.
support.recording.title: Recording will not start
support.recording.body: Check permissions and the microphone at the top of Settings → Voice input. System default is an input device, not system playback capture. Failed capture or missing audio callbacks cancels quietly: reconnect the device and start again. If the macOS audio driver itself stops responding, quit and reopen Talkless. A flashing indicator alone does not prove audio arrived.
support.model.title: The model is not ready
support.model.body: Open Settings → Voice input and finish downloading and preparing the local model, or check the Doubao Speech key, resource and network. On macOS 26, use a current app version: older betas had an incompatible Metal library. Updating the app does not require deleting or downloading your model again.
support.text.title: Text went missing or landed elsewhere
support.text.body: Keep the intended field focused. Current versions no longer block later dictations because a clipboard-read callback was missing. If text still fails to arrive, note whether ordinary typing works and whether the result appeared in the overlay; recover it from History. Include the browser/app and whether the failure occurs while appending to an unsent message.
support.ai.title: AI is unavailable
support.ai.body: Check provider, key and model in Settings → AI polishing. Test Connection sends a fixed sample and may incur provider charges. AI polishing times out after five seconds and quietly uses the recognized text; this does not limit audio capture or recognition. Labs adds dual-engine and candidate-selection waits. Diagnostics separates these stages. Never share an API key in a report.
support.report.title: Report a reproducible problem
support.report.body: Use the GitHub repository link in the header, then choose Issues. Include your Talkless version and build, macOS version, Mac model, speech engine, microphone and clear steps to reproduce. Say what you expected and what actually happened. This website does not collect or submit reports.
support.report.diagnostics: If diagnostics would help, use Settings → System → Diagnostics to export a local ZIP. Review its contents before attaching it; optional crash reports may include personal information and file paths. Nothing is automatically uploaded. Avoid sharing private dictation or selected text.

guide.labs.title: Optional experiments
guide.labs.body: Settings → Labs contains Enhanced recognition and Sentence alternatives, both off by default. Enhanced recognition sends the same audio to local Qwen and Doubao, then gives the available transcripts to your AI service. It requires the local model, Doubao credentials and an AI service; one failed route stops while the other continues. It can use more resources and take longer; improved accuracy is not guaranteed.
guide.labs.choices: Sentence alternatives appears only when AI returns two or three different full versions. Changed words are highlighted. Click a whole sentence; hover to pause the countdown and leave to resume. Timeout uses the marked default. The wait defaults to five seconds and can be set from two to fifteen. Explicit same-language choices can feed dictionary learning; timeout is not user approval.
release.note.0: Removed clipboard-read detection that could block later dictations. Each paste now settles after a finite two-second compatibility interval and releases its state.
release.note.1: Clipboard restoration respects user changes. Sending paste keys is not a guarantee that the target accepted the text.
privacy.provider.body: Volcengine is a third-party provider relative to Talkless. Its general Terms of Service and Privacy Policy name Beijing Volcano Engine Technology Co., Ltd. The applicable contract and product-specific terms are those presented when you activate or purchase the Speech service in the Volcengine console. See the official documents below; API documentation is not a user agreement.
privacy.provider.scope: Talkless’s statement that it does not save recordings describes Talkless itself, not a promise about Volcengine’s retention or training policies. The provider distinguishes customer data processed by its services from account personal information. Consult the applicable service terms for processing, retention and deletion; this page does not claim zero retention or no training by the provider.
guide.speech.provider: Doubao online means Volcengine’s Doubao Speech ASR service. Obtain a Speech API key in the Volcengine console, not a Doubao app login or an Ark chat-model key. It is an optional third-party service; the official terms are linked on our privacy page.
